title: Free-common-input key collision on seven-round AES-192, QBD 2025 full version

target.description: Initial AddRoundKey, six full rounds, then a final round without MixColumns; standard AES-192 key expansion. The same freely selected input is used under both keys.

setting.key_relation: The adversary constructs two distinct keys and one common input; there is no secret-key oracle.
assumptions: The attacker can choose the common plaintext/chaining value.
Equal AES ciphertexts at that common input also yield equal Davies-Meyer outputs after XOR with the same input.
The DM interpretation is semi-free-start and does not prescribe a fixed hash IV.

time.note: Expected collision work in the source inbound/outbound cost model; no conversion to full-AES encryption units is made.

data.note: No independent external-oracle data budget is specified for the offline construction.

memory.note: Table 1 prints a dash; a quantitative storage bound was not extracted.

preprocessing.note: No separate reusable preprocessing budget is reported.

success.description: The source prices expected work for one collision, not a numerical probability of finding at least one at that fixed budget. Inbound DDT characteristic probability is distinct from the GD-generated starting-point distribution; outbound probability is conditional on an admissible inbound point. Published witness pairs and implementation timings are not a trial-denominated experimental success rate.

review.scope: Exact-edition targeted success audit of defining constructions and parameter-specific cost/probability passages; not a new full-paper/forward audit. Weak-key/structure fractions, local false matches, raw Grover marked fractions and whole-attack success stay distinct.

components.description: PDF52–57 AppendixD.2: source inbound characteristic model, not the probability that the GD procedure generates a starting point or the whole attack succeeds.
PDF52–57 AppendixD.2: source outbound characteristic conditioned on a conforming starting point. Sufficient degrees of freedom or expected one collision does not quantify finite-budget success.

evidence.locator: Table 1 p.6, AES-192 DM semi-free-start row; Section 7 p.29; Appendix D.2 p.57; Table 7 p.36, first pair; author verifier lines 338-380.
evidence.interpretation: The free-common-input key collision is equivalent to the stated semi-free-start DM collision. Table 7 supplies the raw AES ciphertext; the verifier computes DM output as ciphertext XOR plaintext.

limitations: The local check verifies one pair and its feedforward output, not search cost or attack success statistics.
A free-common-input seven-round result cannot replace a fixed-zero-input result, or a fixed-IV hash collision claim.
